ground_truth.node_text: Attach a triaxial accelerometer to the spindle nose using a flat washer stud or epoxy mount with the sensor axes aligned to the machine X, Y, and Z axes. Repeat the measurement at the maximum rated speed and compare all six readings against the baseline vibration record from the previous service.

ground_truth.node_text: Apply a thin uniform coat of Prussian blue or engineer's marking compound to the taper surface of a clean test arbor. Insert the arbor into the spindle taper bore and rotate by hand under moderate axial load for two to three turns. Withdraw the arbor and inspect the transfer pattern; uniform contact over at least 75% of the taper length is required. A patchy or one sided pattern indicates taper bore damage, swarf contamination, or arbor misalignment.

ground_truth.node_text: Fit a sealed test arbor with a coolant pressure gauge and flow indicator into the spindle taper. Start the coolant through spindle circuit at the normal operating pressure. Read the pressure gauge at the spindle taper outlet and compare against the minimum required coolant through spindle pressure. Observe the flow indicator for steady flow; pulsing or absent flow indicates a blocked spindle check valve or a failing coolant pump.

turns.utterance: Load the test piece material into the machine work holding and run the standard spindle test machining program. After machining, measure bore diameter at three depths and face flatness at four points using a coordinate measuring machine or precision gauges.

ground_truth.node_text: Load the test piece material, typically a 100 millimetre diameter aluminium or cast iron disc, into the machine work holding and run the standard spindle test machining program. The program bores a 50 millimetre diameter hole and faces the top surface. After machining, measure bore diameter at three depths and face flatness at four points using a coordinate measuring machine or precision gauges. Compare all results against the machined geometry tolerances in the spindle acceptance test plan.

turns.utterance: Test piece machined and measurements taken at all specified points.

ground_truth.node_text: Load the test piece material, typically a 100 millimetre diameter aluminium or cast iron disc, into the machine work holding and run the standard spindle test machining program. The program bores a 50 millimetre diameter hole and faces the top surface. After machining, measure bore diameter at three depths and face flatness at four points using a coordinate measuring machine or precision gauges. Compare all results against the machined geometry tolerances in the spindle acceptance test plan.

issues.original: No, the pressure is below specification and flow appears irregular.
issues.corrected: No, the pressure and flow are not within specification.
issues.explanation: The operator's response characterizes the flow as 'irregular' which implies knowledge of what 'steady flow' should look like and suggests diagnostic reasoning about pump or valve issues. This is premature—the operator should simply report whether the readings meet specification or not, without inferring root causes that belong to downstream troubleshooting steps.
